matters:
Today is decision day: the FOMC's rate announcement is due at 14:00 ET, followed by Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference at 14:30 ET. Fed funds futures put the odds of a quarter-point hike at roughly 92% as of Wednesday morning, per Yahoo Finance's live markets coverage — still a near-lock, though a touch below Tuesday's 94.5% reading this brief cited yesterday. It would be the Fed's first hike since July 2023. The blackout that began 5 September holds until the announcement, so no official has been able to respond on the record to any of the past 24 hours of news before then.

Equity futures point modestly higher ahead of the vote — Dow futures +0.15%, S&P 500 futures +0.16%, Nasdaq-100 futures +0.20%, Russell 2000 futures +0.12%, per Yahoo Finance — a reversal from Tuesday, when all three major indexes closed lower for a third straight session: the Dow fell 328.09 points (−0.63%) to 52,093.11, the S&P 500 fell 0.45% to 7,585.73, and the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.78% to 25,981.57, pressured by the 10-year Treasury yield's close at 5.01%, the highest since 2007.

The oil-pipeline story split further rather than resolved. U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright told CNBC on the sidelines of a G20 energy meeting in Houston on Tuesday that the Saudi East-West pipeline outage would be “measured in days” — a more specific restatement of the “soon” framing this brief flagged as the optimistic outlier on Monday. Reuters sources briefed on the damage continue to estimate three to six weeks, and the pipeline itself remains offline with Saudi Arabia routing some exports back through Hormuz with U.S. military support. Neither estimate has been tested against an actual reopening yet.

The AI-slowdown story stayed political rather than monetary. China's state-run Global Times ran an editorial on 14 September branding Dario Amodei's call for an industry slowdown a “Cold War playbook” that would “significantly increase the trial-and-error costs and risks of loss of control in global AI development” if it excluded China — a sharper, state-media echo of foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun's “fear-mongering” comment already in this brief's record, and a second Chinese voice this week arguing the same position President Trump has taken from the opposite side.

On the financing thread this brief has tracked since 10 September, no new debt-financed sponsor buyout has printed since Sequence Holdings and Michael Dell's DFO Management agreed to take Baldwin Group private on 14 September — itself mostly equity and assumed debt, not fresh leverage. That test now carries into the Fed's decision itself with no cleaner candidate having emerged overnight.

Invalidation: with odds already priced above 90%, anything short of the fully-priced 25bp hike — a smaller move, a split vote, or dovish language in the Summary of Economic Projections — risks an outsized reaction precisely because so little probability is left on the other side.

regime.sizing: Odds of today's 25bp hike sit around 92%, just below Tuesday's 94.5%, so the Summary of Economic Projections and Warsh's press conference remain the swing factors rather than the vote itself. The pipeline dispute between Wright's 'days' framing and Reuters' three-to-six week reporting is still unresolved with the line itself still offline.

secondOrder: Four threads are running into the vote, and none of them resolved overnight. The Fed thread held steady rather than firming further: odds eased slightly from 94.5% Tuesday to roughly 92% Wednesday morning, still a near-lock but no longer tightening the way it was through Monday and Tuesday. The oil thread got a second, more specific data point on the optimistic side: Wright's Monday 'soon' became Tuesday's 'measured in days,' a firmer claim that will be easier to judge right or wrong once it comes due, but Reuters' three-to-six week sourcing hasn't moved and the pipeline hasn't reopened. The AI thread picked up a second Chinese voice: Global Times' state-media 'Cold War playbook' editorial adds an ideological framing beyond the foreign ministry's practical 'fear-mongering' dismissal, which matters because it signals the story has state-media sanction in Beijing, not just a spokesperson's line. And the financing thread stayed exactly where it was: no new debt-financed buyout has printed since Baldwin on 14 September, so the test set on 10 September now runs out the clock against the Fed's own decision.

scorecard.text: The 15 September brief treated the AI-slowdown story as detached from Fed policy. That held again: China's state-run Global Times ran a 14 September editorial calling Dario Amodei's proposal a “Cold War playbook,” a second Chinese voice (beyond the foreign ministry's earlier “fear-mongering” line) arguing the same position from the opposite side as President Trump — still two governments, not central bankers, driving the story, with zero linkage to Wednesday's rate decision.

The financing test set on 10 September — a large, freshly debt-financed sponsor buyout printing before the Fed votes — is still open. No new candidate has emerged since Sequence Holdings/DFO's mostly-equity purchase of Baldwin Group on 14 September, and the test now runs directly into today's 14:00 ET decision with nothing left to close it beforehand.

The 15 September brief treated Reuters' three-to-six week pipeline estimate as more credible than the U.S. energy secretary's optimism. Tuesday sharpened rather than settled that split: Chris Wright told CNBC in Houston the outage would be “measured in days,” a firmer claim than Monday's “soon,” while Reuters' sourcing hasn't moved and the pipeline remains offline. Neither side has been tested against an actual reopening yet.
